lines: אֵין מַחְסֶה מָתוֹק זוּלָתְךָ לְנֶפֶשׁ דַּלָּה
הוֹי בַּעַל הַצַּד הַפָּצוּעַ, אֲדֹן הַחֶסֶד
אֶלְבַּשׁ אֶת־הַגּוּף הַנֶּהְדָּר, אֵדַע בְּלִי גְּבוּל

review: Every stanza ends on the vocative يَا سَيِّدِي يَسُوع ('O Master Jesus'); the Hebrew keeps it word for word as אֲדֹנִי יֵשׁוּעַ, except the last stanza, where the Arabic itself turns it into 'the love of my Master Jesus', so 4:4 follows the Arabic.
1:1 נָתַתָּ דָּם — 'You gave blood'; the Arabic بَذَلْتَ لِي الدَّمَ is 'You poured out blood for me', and Hebrew keeps the short form because the line already runs long.
2:1 לְנֶפֶשׁ דַּלָּה — 'for the weak soul', for لِمُهْجَةِ الضَّعِيف; the Arabic مُهْجَة is 'life-blood/heart', which Hebrew renders with נֶפֶשׁ because it is the psalm word for the inner life.

3:1–3:2 הַמֵּנִיחַ … הַצַּד הַפָּצוּעַ — the Arabic الْمُرِيح … الْجَنْبِ الْجَرِيح is 'restful … the wounded side'; the spear-wound of John 19:34 is kept as צַד פָּצוּעַ, and הַמֵּנִיחַ is the hiph'il of נוח used for giving rest.
4:3 אֵדַע בְּלִי גְּבוּל — 'I shall know without limit', for سَأَعْرِفُ بِلَا حُدُود; the phrase is kept because the Arabic deliberately contrasts the bounded body with boundless knowing.
